fieldValues.title: migrate_carrier and its sibling migrations still silently accept partial-write risk on a bare on-disk FileStore
fieldValues.summary: srs-rust#1015 made the RepositoryStore batch seam honest (abort_batch now refuses rather than lying) but deliberately did not gate migrate_carrier / migrate_discovery_query_cutover / migrate_composition_cutover / migrate_identity_service on the new supports_batch_rollback() capability, because doing so unconditionally would break ~10+ existing tests and disable these migrations in production (they run almost entirely against .srsj/MemVfs-backed sessions with no escape-hatch option struct, unlike rfc038_storage_migration_service which already has StorageMigrationOptions.allow_non_atomic).
fieldValues.rationale: srs-rust#1018 proposes the fix: give each of these functions the same allow_non_atomic-style opt-in that rfc038_storage_migration_service already has, gated on !store.supports_batch_rollback(), with every existing test/CLI call site passing allow_non_atomic: true to preserve current behavior. Any future unit touching these four migration services, or reasoning about #813's remaining scope, should read srs-rust#1018 before assuming the batch seam is fixed for them — only the trait-level honesty (abort_batch's return value) is fixed; the actual up-front refusal is not yet wired into any of the four migration functions themselves.
